messages:
maria-sdk: heads up — hit a weird parity bug in kotlin SDK around retry/backoff + coroutine cancellation. appears only on Android API 29 emulator.

maria-sdk: root case: auth refresh triggers a retry but the original call's coroutine gets cancelled and okhttp connection/queue ends up stalling. app-level callback never returns.

nina-qa: repro steps? can run locally if small checklist provided.

maria-sdk: simple repro attached inline:
```
val call = api.generate(...)
call.await() // suspending
// on 401, AuthInterceptor enqueues refresh and then retries original request
```
logs:
```
I/OkHttp: --> POST /v1/complete
W/Auth: refresh started
I/OkHttp: <-- 401
I/Auth: refresh done
I/OkHttp: --> POST /v1/complete (retry)
// then nothing, coroutine hung
```

maria-sdk: observed that call.cancel() doesn't always free dispatcher threads; after ~6 retries the client's dispatcher.workQueue seems blocked.

ajay-eng: @maria-sdk can you paste the interceptor snippet? curious if we're doing synchronous refresh on IO thread.

maria-sdk: here's simplified interceptor:
```
override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
  val req = chain.request()
  val resp = chain.proceed(req)
  if (resp.code == 401) {
    runBlocking { tokenRefresher.refresh() } // sync block on interceptor thread
    val newReq = req.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer ${tokenRefresher.token}").build()
    return chain.proceed(newReq)
  }
  return resp
}
```

ajay-eng: aha — runBlocking inside intercept is sketchy on Android + OkHttp because it can tie up dispatcher threads used by the connection pool. try using a non-blocking approach or pre-refresh before the request.

nina-qa: we saw similar in other repos but thought it was emulator-only. @sam-devex-bot do we have any flaky test incidents referencing "hung okhttp" in last 30 days?

sam-devex-bot: incident-search: found 2 hits — "okhttp-hang-after-retry" (2024-09-11) and "auth-refresh-stall" (2024-12-03). links: https://intranet/incidents/okhttp-hang, https://intranet/incidents/auth-refresh-stall

maria-sdk: interesting — worked around by switching to asynchronous refresh path:
```
val refreshDeferred = coroutineScope.async { tokenRefresher.refresh() }
val token = refreshDeferred.await()
val newReq = req.newBuilder().header("Authorization","Bearer $token").build()
return chain.proceed(newReq)
```
but still uneasy — need parity guarantee between Java and Kotlin SDKs on how interceptors handle retries + cancellation.

ajay-eng: agree. action items: (1) avoid runBlocking in interceptor (2) add a lightweight test harness that simulates cancellation mid-retry on emulator farm (3) doc note on SDK parity for auth interceptor behavior.

nina-qa: I'll add a flaky test job that hits the emulator matrix (API 28-31) and toggles cancellation during retry. can we also add a guard in the Kotlin SDK to cap retry attempts and surface a clear error instead of hanging?

maria-sdk: yes — cap to 3 and fallback to 503 with structured error explaining "retry cancelled due to token refresh conflict".

ajay-eng: pinging @platform about adding connection-pool metrics to make it easier to spot dispatcher stalls. ops-bot, any thoughts?

ops-bot: noted — instrumenting okhttp.dispatcher.queuedCalls and runningCalls counts in the console telemetry next week.

maria-sdk: thanks all. I'll open a PR with the interceptor fix + a small unit harness and link the flaky test in the PR description. :thumbsup:

ajay-eng: cheers — will review.

nina-qa: leaving a quick test note in the ticket so we can validate before shipping.

maria-sdk: filing now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-kotlin/issues/842
